items.text: The International Space Station has been always closed to the public, and NASA previously was strongly against allowing tourists and commercial interest on the ISS. Commercial activity so far has been limited to science experiments. However, the agency’s chief financial officer told reporters that commercialising the station will enable NASA ‘to focus resources’ to land the next man and the first woman on the moon by 2024. NASA now has declared parts of the ISS open for business – it will let private astronauts visit and stay as early as next year, will allow in-space manufacturing, health care research and even marketing. Also, back in May, the Trump administration said that it would ask Congress to add $1.6 billion to NASA’s budget next year to help finance NASA’s plans to send astronauts back to the moon. Difficult words: chief financial officer (the boss of the finances in a company), declare (officially say that something is now true), budget (finances, money, financial plan). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The International Space Station was always closed to the public, and NASA was strongly against tourists and business there. The only commercial activity was limited to science experiments. However, things are changing because NASA wants to land the next man and the first woman on the moon by 2024 and it needs money to do that. To help fund the future mission, NASA recently declared parts of the ISS open for business. Private astronauts will be able to visit and stay as early as next year. There is also going to be more research on the ISS. Difficult words: fund (finance, pay for), declare (officially say that something is now true), research (studying something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The International Space Station was closed to the public . Only astronauts from some countries could go there. Now, NASA is making big changes. It is opening the ISS to people. More business will be done on the ISS, too. Astronauts will study more things there. Difficult words: was (past of ‘is’), public (people), could (past of ‘can’), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Countries around the world are working to launch 5G networks, and China’s Huawei is one of the few companies that makes 5G-compatible equipment. The US government blacklisted Huawei as a threat to national security, but the Russian government made a deal with the company to develop the new network in its country. Chinese President Xi Jinping finalised the deal when he visited Russia – it was one of many struck agreements, which are worth over $20 billion in total. Difficult words: launch (build, start), blacklist (ban, put an embargo on), strike–struck (achieve, successfully come to). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Countries around the world are working to build 5G networks. China’s Huawei is one of the few companies which makes 5G equipment . The USA banned Huawei because the American government sees it as a threat to its security. On the other hand, Russia made a deal with Huawei that it is going to build a 5G network in Russia. When the Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Russia, he finalised the deal with Putin. They made many deals, and the total worth of the deals is more than $20 billion. Difficult words: equipment (technology, machines), deal (a plan to work together on something), threat (a danger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Countries are building 5G networks. A few companies make 5G equipment . Chinese company Huawei is one of them. The USA bans Huawei. The USA says that it is a dangerous company. Russia makes a deal with Huawei. Huawei is going to build a 5G network in Russia. The Chinese President Xi Jinping visits Russia. Putin and he make the deal final. They make many deals. They are all worth more than $20 billion. Difficult words: equipment (technology, machines), deal (a plan to work together on something), be worth (have a price in money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has exceeded 2,000 cases since last August. People confirmed more than 1,900 cases and 94 probable cases. The outbreak is the second largest on record, and it has killed around 1,300 people. The director of the World Health Organisation says that it wants to end the outbreak, but there have been problems. Some people do not trust the vaccine, there are conflicts in some regions, and 130 attacks have happened against Doctors Without Borders. Difficult words: outbreak (a sudden large ‘happening’ of an illness), exceed (be more than), confirmed (something confirmed really happened). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There is an Ebola outbreak in Congo, and from August 2018 until now, there are more than 2,000 cases of the illness . This is the second largest outbreak and around 1,300 people are dead so far. The World Health Organisation wants to end the outbreak, but there are problems. Some people do not trust the vaccine, there can be conflicts in some regions and sometimes people attack doctors. Doctors Without Borders had 130 attacks. Difficult words: outbreak (a sudden large ‘happening’ of an illness), case (a situation when someone has a sickness), illness (a sickness – when bacteria or virus make you feel very bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is Ebola in Congo. Ebola is a serious sickness. From August 2018 until now, 2,000 people catch it. Around 1,300 people die. The World Health Organisation is trying to stop Ebola. It is not easy. There are some problems. People are fighting in some areas. Some people do not want to be vaccinated . Sometimes, people attack doctors. Doctors Without Borders had 130 attacks. Difficult words: until (to), vaccinate (give a special type of medicine called an injection so that people do not catch a sickness), had (past tense of ‘have’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to a new study, protected land is shrinking around the world, and the USA under President Trump has seen its largest reduction ever. However, the study says that 90% of the government’s proposed land protection changes have been issued since 2000. Trump is also not the first president to shrink a national monument (which in the USA is a protected area similar to a national park). For example, three different presidents shrank Mount Olympus National Monument in Washington before it eventually was designated a national park. Across the globe, 1.3 million square miles of land protections have been downgraded or removed since 1961, according to the study. The changes are largely in favour of industrial operations, but local pressure and land claims are also a cause. Difficult words: shrink–shrank (get smaller), issue (put out), land claim (saying that some land is yours or asking for it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new study found out that protected land around the world is shrinking . Under President Trump, the USA saw the largest reduction in protected land ever. However, the study says that government proposed 90% of the changes since 2000. Trump is also not the first president to reduce protected land. For example, three American presidents shrank some protected land in Washington. Around the world, 1.3 million square miles were reduced since 1961. The changes are mostly because of industry. Difficult words: shrink (get smaller), reduction (the action of reducing – to reduce something means to make something smaller), propose (say that you want to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists do a study . They watch how much protected land there is. There is less and less protected land. From 1961 to 2019, there are 1.3 million square miles less of protected land. This is mostly because of industry . In the USA, there is less and less protected land, too. Difficult words: study noun (a science ‘project’ which gets information about something), protected land (for example, land which is only for animals and people cannot build there), industry (a big business, especially the type which is bad for animals and plants because it is very dirty). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This year is the 30th anniversary of the student-led 1989 Tiananmen Square protests which called for democracy, human rights, and an end to corruption in China. Ahead of the anniversary, China’s defence minister said that the violent response to the protests was the right move, arguing that it helped bring ‘stability’ to the country during a politically turbulent time. It is not known how many were injured and wounded in the crackdown exactly, but people say that the number of dead range from several hundred to several thousand people. The US Secretary of State , Mike Pompeo, called the actions of the protesters ‘heroic’ and criticised China’s history of human rights abuses . One of the examples that he gave was China’s recent arrests of over 1 million Muslims. Difficult words: turbulent (very unstable), crackdown (repression, serious action against something), Secretary of State (a person in the government who represents the USA in international things), abuse (an act of not respecting the human rights). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 1989, the Tiananmen Square protests were protests for democracy and human rights in China. The Chinese government responded violently to these protests. It is not known how many people died, but people say that it is something between a few hundred to a few thousand of people. Now it is 30 years after the events at Tiananmen Square. Recently, China’s defence minister said that the violent response was the right move and that it was good for the stability of the country. The US Secretary of State also talked about the Tiananmen Square protests. He said that the protesters were heroes, and he criticised China for not respecting the human rights. One of the examples that he gave was that China arrested more than 1 million Muslims recently. Difficult words: human rights (for example, the idea that all people are free and that it is not OK to kill people), respond (answer, do something because of something else), violently (by fighting), Secretary of State (a person in the government who represents the USA in international events). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tiananmen Square is in Beijing in China. In 1989, some people protest there. They want democracy and human rights . The Chinese government does not want these protests. They attack the people. Many people die. Now it is 30 years after these events. Some people talk about the Tiananmen Square protests. One man from the Chinese government says that attacking the people was good. One man from the American government says that the protesters were heroes. He says that China does not respect human rights. Difficult words: human rights (the idea that all people are free and that it is not OK to kill people, for example), government (the ‘bosses’ of a country), was, were (past of ‘is’ and ‘are’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

07-06-19 15:00 A woman was pregnant with her baby at 23 weeks (about 6 months) when she felt very uncomfortable. She thought that it was part of her pregnancy, but it was preeclampsia and her blood pressure was extremely high. The baby had to be born quickly, and doctors said that the baby girl would not survive. However, she survived past the first hour into six months. A nurse said that the workers did everything that they could, but it is always up to the babies to be strong outside the womb . The baby’s mother said that the nurses helped her a lot while her baby grew in the hospital. The mother said that ‘she is the smallest baby, but she’s mine’. Difficult words: preeclampsia (a serious problem that happens when a pregnant woman’s blood pressure rises very high; it can damage the woman and the baby’s organs), womb (the part of the woman’s body where the baby grows inside). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

07-06-19 15:00 A woman was pregnant with her baby at 23 weeks (about 6 months) when she did not feel well. She thought that it was part of her pregnancy, but it was preeclampsia and her blood pressure was very high. The baby had to be born soon, and doctors said that the baby girl would not survive. However, the baby is alive today after six months. A nurse said that the workers help the babies as much as they can, but the babies have to be strong outside the womb . The mother says that ‘she is the smallest baby, but she’s mine’. Difficult words: preeclampsia (a serious problem that pregnant women can get that can hurt the woman and the baby’s organs), blood pressure (how much the blood presses in the body – this is important medical information), womb (where the baby grows inside its mother). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

07-06-19 15:00 A woman is pregnant. Her baby is 23 weeks old. That is about 6 months old. The mother does not feel well. She goes to hospital. She has preeclampsia . The baby must be born very early. The baby is not ready to leave her mother’s body. Doctors say that the baby will not live. However, the baby girl lives. She is six months old now. A nurse says that all nurses help the premature babies . The babies have to be very strong to live. The mother says that her baby is the smallest baby. She is her baby. Difficult words: preeclampsia (a serious problem that pregnant women sometimes have), will (in the future), premature baby (a baby born early). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA selected three companies to help it get back to the moon. The companies, Astrobotic, Intuitive Machines and Orbit Beyond, will provide lunar landing services which will deliver science and research cargo to the moon as part of a program called Artemis. NASA aims to return astronauts to the moon by 2024, and the agency sees these commercial landers as the first step toward that. If everything goes according to plan, the space agency hopes to have a sustained human presence on the moon by 2028. Difficult words: lunar (related to the moon). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA wants to return astronauts to the moon by 2024. Three companies, Astrobotic, Intuitive Machines and Orbit Beyond, are going to help NASA with the plan. They are going to provide lunar landing services which will deliver cargo . All of this is part of a program called Artemis. If everything goes according to plan, NASA hopes to have a sustained human presence on the moon by 2028. Difficult words: lunar (about the moon), cargo (things that you bring to another place), sustained human presence (a place where people can live). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA wants to go back to the moon. It wants to go there in 2024. NASA chooses three companies. The companies are going to help NASA. They are going to help move things to the moon. If everything goes OK, NASA plans to move people to the moon. It wants people to live on the moon by 2028. Difficult words: are going to (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Rio de Janeiro, police killed 558 people between January and April this year – that is 89 more people than in the same period last year. A total of 1,534 people were killed by police in Rio in 2018. This year’s number is the highest ever. Brazil had programs to reduce the number of police killings, but there was no money for the programs when the country faced an economic and political crisis five years ago. Since then, the number of people killed by police has increased. The New York Times says that there is more crime because of gangs. In 2018, people elected candidates who want to allow police officers to shoot armed suspects . Rio’s governor said that these kinds of laws can help. On the other hand, the Human Rights Watch wants to reduce police killings in Rio. It says that police killings are making the fight against crime worse because people are scared of police. Since 2015, 72 police officers were charged with homicide . Difficult words: elect (vote for/choose), armed suspect (a criminal with a gun), homicide (the killing of one person by another). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Police in Rio de Janeiro killed 558 people from January to April of this year. That is 89 more people than in January to April of last year. A total of 1,534 people were killed by police in Rio in 2018. This year’s number is the highest ever. Brazil had programs to reduce the number of police killings, but there was no money for these programs. The number of people killed by the police is going up. The New York Times says that there is more crime in Rio because of gangs. Rio’s governor wants police to have more power to shoot more criminals to make people safe. Others think that people will get scared of police and crime will get worse. Since 2015, 72 police officers were charged with homicide . Difficult words: governor (the city leader), charge (formally say that somebody did something illegal), homicide (the killing of one person by another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. The city has a crime problem. People shoot and kill people. From January to April of 2018, police kill 469 people. It is worse this year. From January to April of 2019, police kill 558 people. In all of 2018, police kill 1534 people in Rio. The New York Times says that there are gangs in Rio. They are the problem. They make the city bad. Some people think that it is good that the police kill the criminals. They think that the police stop the criminals by killing them. Other people think that this is not good. They think that good people can be scared of police. Difficult words: gang (an organised groups of criminals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The governor of the American state of Colorado signed a law last Friday which made Colorado the 18th state (out of 50) to ban gay conversion therapy for minors . Conversion therapy is a practice of trying to change an individual’s sexual orientation from homosexual or bisexual to heterosexual. The law prohibits psychiatrists or other professionals to participate in “conversion therapy” to change a minor’s sexual orientation or gender identity. Those who break the law will be subject to disciplinary measures . The governor tweeted that ‘so-called conversion therapy is a torturous practice that has long been widely- discredited by medical and mental health professionals.’ Difficult words: minor (a person younger than 18), disciplinary measures (action which is taken when a worker does something wrong – they can be ordered to stop working), torturous (like torture – painful and cruel), discredit (to prove that something is wrong). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Conversion therapy is a practice of trying to change an individual’s sexual orientation from homosexual or bisexual to heterosexual. Last Friday, Colorado became the 18th American state (out of 50) to ban it. The new law prohibits psychiatrists or other professionals from doing the therapy with people who are minors . Difficult words: ban (make something illegal – people must not do it), prohibit (stop), minor (a person younger than 18). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Most people are heterosexual. This means that women like men or men like women. Some people are homosexual. A homosexual man likes men. A homosexual woman likes women. Some people do conversion therapy. Conversion therapy tries to change homosexual people into heterosexual people. Conversion therapy is legal in most American states. Colorado bans the therapy . People cannot do conversion therapy on minors in Colorado. Colorado becomes the 18th state to ban conversion therapy. Difficult words: legal (people can do legal things), ban (make something illegal – people must not do it), minor (a person younger than 18). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least seven people died after a sightseeing boat capsized and sank on the Danube River in Budapest last Wednesday. People say that those they found dead were not wearing life jackets. Thirty-five people were on board the boat when it crashed into another vessel during a rainstorm. Several people were saved but as of Thursday afternoon, 21 passengers were still missing. Apart from two Hungarian crew members, all of the passengers were South Korean tourists. South Korea’s Foreign Ministry said that the country was sending its own rescue workers to help search for survivors. Difficult words: capsize (overturn), vessel (a boat). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Budapest, Hungary a sightseeing boat on the Danube River crashed into another boat last Wednesday. It capsized , sank and more than seven people died. The seven bodies did not have life jackets. On Thursday afternoon, 21 passengers were still missing . All of the passengers were South Korean tourists. Difficult words: sightseeing (for seeing sights – things which tourists want to see), capsize (turn over), be missing (when a person is missing, we do not know if they are OK and where they are). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Budapest. Budapest is the capital of Hungary. A river runs through the city. There are boats on the river. There are 35 people on one boat. Thirty-three of them are tourists. They are from South Korea. This boat hits another boat. It turns over . It sinks . People find 7 dead bodies. Twenty-one people are missing . Difficult words: turn over (when the up goes down and down goes up), sink (go down), be missing (when a person is missing, we do not know if they are OK and where they are). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For the first time in 40 years, high-ranking Taiwanese and American officials met last month. Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry confirmed the meeting by the end of May, saying they discussed ‘common security challenges’. A spokesman for China’s Foreign Ministry expressed ‘strong dissatisfaction ’ and asked the USA to ‘ abide by the one-China principle’ and stop official communication with Taiwan. China sees Taiwan as part of its territory even though the island is its own country. Difficult words: confirm (say that something is true), dissatisfaction (being dissatisfied – unhappy/angry about something), abide (conform to, follow). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last month, Taiwanese and American officials met for the first time in 40 years. Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry confirmed the meeting. The ministry said that they discussed security. China’s Foreign Ministry was not happy about the meeting. Taiwan is a country separate from China, but China sees it as its territory. The speaker for the Chinese ministry asked the USA not to talk to Taiwan. China’s Foreign Ministry asked the USA to act by the ‘one-China principle’. Difficult words: official (a person who works for the government – the bosses of a country), confirm (say that something is true), separate (different, not part of China). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Taiwanese and American officials meet. It is the first USA–Taiwan meeting in 40 years. Taiwan says that security is discussed at the meeting. China is not happy about the meeting. It does not see Taiwan as a separate country. It sees Taiwan as its territory. Taiwan feels differently. China asks the USA not to talk to Taiwan. Difficult words: official (a person who works for the government – the bosses of a country), security (safety – how safe a country is, usually safe from other countries), separate (different from, not part of China). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The 2019 European Parliament election took place from May 23rd to May 26th and it was the first time that voter participation increased since 1979. Around 400 million Europeans were eligible and about 51% participated in the elections, putting the number of those who voted somewhere near 203 million. People expected nationalist parties to make large gains and they did. About one quarter of the available seats were won by them for the first time ever. However, pro-EU mainstream parties maintained dominance with 507 seats out of the parliament’s total 751. Difficult words: participation (the act of participating – to participate means to do something), eligible (able to vote). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The election in the European Parliament happened from May 23rd to May 26th. Around 400 million Europeans were eligible to vote and 51% of them did. That is around 203 million people. People thought that nationalist parties would get a lot of votes and they did. For the first time ever, they won one quarter of the seats in the parliament. However, pro-EU parties still hold most seats – 507 out of the total 751. Difficult words: election (a situation when people elect/vote for/choose their leaders), eligible (able to vote), seat (a place in the parliament). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People hold election for the European Parliament. The election happens from May 23rd to May 26th. Around 400 million Europeans can vote. This year, around 51% of them vote. That is around 203 million people. Most people vote for pro-EU parties . These parties get 507 out of 751 seats in the parliament. Some people vote for nationalist parties. Nationalist parties usually do not like the EU. They usually want their country to be strong. Around 25% of people vote for nationalist parties. Difficult words: election (a situation when people elect/vote for/choose their leaders), party (a political group), seat (a place in the parliament). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to a report from the University of Cambridge, Coca Cola can review and possibly repress information from its health research. It can also stop research if the findings are ‘ unfavourable’ . This could lead to publication bias which is something that happens when someone publishes only studies of their choice. However, the researchers do not believe that Coca Cola has done that yet. Coca Cola says that its scientists have full control over their studies. It says that it does not have the right to stop the publishing of research results. Nevertheless, researchers are worried, and they are asking Coca Cola and other companies to publish lists of their cancelled studies. Difficult words: repress (keep down, keep quiet), unfavourable (not good). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

According to a research report, Coca Cola can review and possibly repress its health research. It can also cancel research if it is not good for the company. This could lead to publication bias . However, the researchers do not think that Coca Cola did this. Coca Cola says that it does not have the right to stop the publishing of studies. Nevertheless, researchers are worried and are asking Coca Cola and other companies to show their lists of cancelled studies. Difficult words: research (a scientific study of something), repress (keep quiet), publication bias (when you only publish/show the things that you want to show to other people to make something look good). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists study Coca Cola. They say that the company does its own studies. They say that it reviews those studies. It can hide the studies that it does not like. It can cancel research that it does not like. This can be a problem. It can mean that people only see the studies that Coca Cola likes. However, Coca Cola says it does not do this. It says that it does not have the right to do this. However, scientists are still worried. They ask Coca Cola and other companies to show their lists of cancelled studies. Difficult words: review (read to see if something is OK), research (a study, finding out information about something very carefully), right (the power to do something), cancelled (not shown). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Billionaire investor Robert F. Smith gave nearly 400 graduating college seniors a gift of a grant to eliminate their student loans. He promised this gift during his 2019 commencement speech for Morehouse College. His great news completely stunned the crowd. One graduate thought that he was lying. The college president said that he had never seen a gift like this before. A representative said that Smith will give $40 million to help pay off the student loans. Each student owes about $48,000 for tuition , housing, and other costs. The college said that many of its students get financial help. For most colleges and universities across the USA, analysts think that student loan debt was about $1.5 trillion last year. Difficult words: commencement (a ceremony when students are given their diplomas), tuition (class costs), debt (money that you owe and have to pay back). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A billionaire investor gave almost 400 graduating college seniors a gift to pay off their student loans . He gave this gift during his 2019 speech at the college. His news shocked the crowd. One graduate thought that he was lying. The college president said that he had never before seen a gift like this. A representative said that the investor will give $40 million to help pay off the student loans. Each student has a loan of about $48,000. For most colleges and universities across the USA, analysts think that student loan debt was about $1.5 trillion last year. Difficult words: investor (a person who invests or spends money in different businesses and then earns money from those businesses), student loan (money that you borrow to go to college or university), student loan debt (the money that you have to pay back after you finish the school). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Almost 400 college students are graduating . A billionaire gives them a gift. He says that he is going to pay off their student loans . People are shocked. One student thinks that the billionaire is lying. The president of the college says that this is the first time that he sees something like this. The billionaire is going to give the students $40 million. Each student has a student loan of around $48,000. In the USA, many college students have student loans. Last year, the student loans are about $1.5 trillion in the USA. Difficult words: college (a school like a university), graduate (finish school and get the diploma), student loan (money that you borrow to go to college, but you must pay it back when you start working). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Ford Motor Company is planning an overall restructuring which involves laying off around 10% of workers worldwide. Ford’s CEO announced the news in an email to employees on Monday 20th. The company plans to spend around $11 billion to restructure its business, which will save it around $600 million every year. Of the 7,000 total jobs being eliminated, roughly 2,300 are in the USA. The whole plan is not known, but some factories in Europe and Brazil are going to close, and the brand has stopped making some of its well-known passenger cars in North America. Difficult words: restructuring (restructure – organise differently), lay off (tell a worker to stop coming to work because you do not need him or her any more), announce (officially say something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Ford Motor Company is planning a big restructuring that will cost the company $11 billion, but it will save it $600 million every year. Some Ford factories in Europe and Brazil are going to close, and Ford will no longer make some cars. Part of the restructuring is laying off around 10% of workers worldwide. Ten per cent is around 7,000 jobs – around 2,300 of those jobs are in the USA. Difficult words: restructuring (restructure – organise differently), lay off (tell a worker to stop coming to work because you do not need him or her any more). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ford is a big car company. It is going through some changes. People are restructuring it. The restructuring costs $11 billion. When it is done, it will save Ford $600 million every year. Ford has around 70,000 employees worldwide. About 10% of them will lose their jobs. The company does not need them anymore. Difficult words: restructure (organise differently), will (in the future), employee (a worker). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Pentagon is part of the military branch of the American government, and Pentagon officials reportedly scheduled to present plans to the White House last Thursday to send up to 10,000 more troops to the Middle East. People say that nothing has been finalised and it is still unclear if the White House will approve the request. The move aims to boost defence in the region, in particular around Iran. The Pentagon also seeks more Patriot missile defence systems, as well as more ships as part of its proposal. The Iran–USA relationship has worsened in the past several weeks. The USA said that Iran mobilised proxy groups to target American forces in Iraq and Syria. Difficult words: boost (make more powerful), mobilise (get ready), proxy groups (groups of soldiers which are ‘friends’ with Iran). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Pentagon is a part of the military in the USA government. People say that Pentagon officials asked the White House to send 10,000 more troops to the Middle East last Thursday. People say that nothing is final and we do not known if the White House will approve this. The Pentagon wants more soldiers, ships and weapons in the area, especially around Iran. The relationship between the USA and Iran is not good at the moment. Difficult words: official (a worker, an officer), troops (soldiers), approve (say ‘yes’ to something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The relationship between the USA and Iran is not good at the moment. The Pentagon is the military part of the USA. People say that the Pentagon wants to send more soldiers to the Middle East. The Pentagon wants to move 10,000 soldiers, ships and weapons there. The Pentagon wants the forces to be around Iran. We do not know if the White House approves this. Difficult words: relationship (how things are between two countries – if they are good or bad), force (soldiers and war machines), approve (say ‘yes’ to something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Botswana is home to 130,000 elephants, which is the most of any country in Africa. In 2014, the government banned hunting of its elephants to help their population grow. Last Wednesday, people lifted the ban on elephant hunting, turning what was once a sanctuary for African elephants into an open territory for licensed hunters. The country plans to grant as many as 400 elephant hunting licenses a year. Botswana’s government said that they lifted the ban because of increasing conflicts between elephants and humans. It says that it has to protect the elephants as well as the people. Difficult words: ban (say that people must not do something), lift (stop), sanctuary (a safe place). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Botswana is home to 130,000 elephants, which is the most of any country in Africa. In 2014, Botswana banned the hunting of elephants to help their population grow. Last Wednesday, people lifted the ban on elephant hunting, and now licensed hunters can hunt elephants again. The country plans to give out up to 400 elephant hunting licenses a year. Botswana explained why it lifted the ban. This was because there were more and more conflicts between people and elephants recently. Botswana said that it must protect its elephants and its people. Difficult words: ban (say that people must not do something), lift (stop), conflict (a problem, a fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Botswana, there are 130,000 elephants. Botswana is the country with the most elephants in Africa. Before 2014, people can hunt elephants in Botswana. Then the country wants to protect the elephants. It bans hunting. Now, there are conflicts between people and elephants. Botswana wants to protect elephants. However, it must protect people, too. Botswana stops the ban. Now people can hunt elephants. However, they must have a licence. Botswana wants to give out up to 400 licenses a year. Difficult words: hunt (shoot/kill), ban (say that people cannot/ must not do something), conflict (problem, fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Theresa May announced her resignation – her leadership of the British Conservative Party will end on June 7th. In her resignation speech, she said that Britain was under stress, but there was so much good about the country, and so much to be proud and optimistic about. She said that serving as prime minister was the honour of her life. After Margaret Thatcher, she was the second female prime minister but certainly, she thinks, not the last. Difficult words: announce (to formally say something), resignation (the act of resigning – to resign means to stop being prime minister), honour (something good which makes you proud). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Theresa May is the British Prime Minister, and she recently gave a speech. She said that she is going to leave office on June 7th. In her speech, she said that Britain is under stress. However, there are many good things about the country, and there is so much to be proud and optimistic about. She said that serving as prime minister was the honour of her life. After Margaret Thatcher, she was the second female prime minister. She thinks that she will not be the last. Difficult words: honour (something good which makes you proud), female (woman). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Theresa May is the British Prime Minister. She gives a speech . She talks about her plans. She says that she is going to step down on June 7th. She says that Britain is under stress now. However, there are many good things about Britain. People still can feel good and be optimistic. She says that for her being prime minister is very special. Difficult words: speech (talk; say something to many people), be going to (in the future), step down (stop being prime minister). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Tuesday was the fifth consecutive day of severe weather in the central states of the USA. According to one government agency, people reported more than 130 tornadoes just in five days. The severe storms reportedly dropped more than 7.62 centimetres of rain in parts of Kansas, Missouri and Oklahoma just last Tuesday. Roads in Oklahoma had to close because of the flooding, and in Missouri, two people reportedly died in a vehicular accident last Tuesday. Difficult words: consecutive (one after another), vehicular (involving vehicles – cars/trucks), affect (make something happen from something else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Recently, the weather in the central states of the USA was so severe that it affected around 28 million people. In just five days, there were more than 130 tornadoes. More than 7.62 centimetres of rain came down in parts of Kansas, Missouri and Oklahoma just last Tuesday. In Oklahoma roads had to close because of flooding . In Missouri, people say that two people died in a road accident. Difficult words: severe (very bad), affect (make something happen), flooding (big water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The USA is a big country. One big region is the central USA. The weather is very bad there. In five days, there are 130 tornadoes. It rains a lot, too. In one day, 7.62 centimetres of rain comes down. The rain floods roads. It affects around 28 million people. Difficult words: flood (go under water), affect (make something happen to someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A weeks-long CNN investigation showed that Houthi rebels have been stealing food provided by the UN from the Yemenis. The UN said last Monday that it is considering stopping aid to Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen. The UN’s program aims to feed around 12 million people in Yemen, which is nearly half of the country’s population, but the UN says that their convoys are blocked. One UN organisation said that around $15 million worth of food does not make it to people who need it each month and that children are dying because of this. The UN is trying to negotiate with Houthi leaders, but talks were not successful. Stopping aid is the last resort, but the organisation said that it would still help children and women. Difficult words: consider (think about), aid (help), negotiate (discuss, talk about). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The United Nations sends food to Yemen to help its people. Sadly, not all of the food gets to them. CNN did an investigation which found out that Houthi rebels are stealing the food. People say that around $15 million worth of food is stolen every month and that children are dying because of this. The UN is trying to negotiate with the Houthi leaders. If the talks are not successful , the UN can stop sending food to Yemen. However, they would still help children and women. Difficult words: negotiate (discuss, talk about), successful (if you are successful in something, you do finish it or make progress). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Yemen has problems. Many Yemenis are hungry. The United Nations helps them. They send them food. However, there is a problem. Not all of the food gets to the people. Houthi rebels take some of the food. They take about $15 million worth of food every month. Children die because of this. The UN is trying to talk to the Houthis. If the talks fail , the UN can stop sending the food. If they stop sending the food, they will still help women and children. Difficult words: worth (have a price in money), fail (go bad), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
